'''Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited''' is an Indian multinational [[automobile manufacturer]], based in [[Mumbai]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tata Motors Re-Enters South Africa Market with Bold, Future-Ready Range of Passenger Vehicles – Tata Motors |url=https://www.tatamotors.com/press-releases/tata-motors-re-enters-south-africa-market-with-bold-future-ready-range-of-passenger-vehicles/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251215232026/https://www.tatamotors.com/press-releases/tata-motors-re-enters-south-africa-market-with-bold-future-ready-range-of-passenger-vehicles/ |archive-date=2025-12-15 |access-date=2026-04-16 |website=www.tatamotors.com |language=en}}</ref> It is a part of [[Tata Group]]. As of 2025, it is the third largest car manufacturer in India by sales, after [[Maruti Suzuki]] and [[Mahindra & Mahindra]] and above [[Hyundai Motor India Limited|Hyundai]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Maruti Suzuki sees 4% growth in January; Hyundai, Tata slip despite Creta & Punch surge |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/auto/cars/maruti-suzuki-sees-4-growth-in-january-hyundai-tata-slip-despite-creta-punch-surge/articleshow/117883344.cms |access-date=6 April 2025 |work=The Times of India |date=3 February 2025}}</ref> It owns British car manufacturer [[Jaguar Land Rover]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=JLR Corporate Homepage International |url=https://media.jaguarlandrover.com/en/news |access-date=2026-04-16 |website=media.jaguarlandrover.com}}</ref>

== History ==
[[File:Tata sier.jpg|thumb|[[Tata Sierra]] (1991-2000)]]
[[File:Tata Sumo EX 2.0 TDi 4x4 2001 (15260028476).jpg|thumb|[[Tata Sumo]] (1994–2019)]]
Tata Motors was founded in 1945, as a [[locomotive]] manufacturer. Tata Motors entered the passenger vehicle market in 1991 with the launch of the [[Tata Sierra]], a multi utility vehicle. This was followed by the launch of the [[Tata Estate]] in 1992 (a [[stationwagon]] based on the existing TataMobile light commercial vehicle) and the [[Tata Sumo]] in 1994, India's first sports utility vehicle.

[[File:Tata Indica DLX front.jpg|thumb|[[Tata Indica]] (first generation)]]

Tata launched the [[Tata Indica|Indica]] in 1998, the first fully indigenous Indian passenger car. Although initially criticised by auto-analysts, its fuel economy, engine and an aggressive marketing strategy made it one of the best selling cars in the history of the Indian automobile industry. A newer version of the car, named Indica V2, was introduced later. Tata Motors also exported the car to South Africa.<ref name="Tata Milestones">{{cite web|url=http://www.tatamotors.com/our_world/rearview.php?version=text|title=Tata Milestones|accessdate=22 March 2009|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20101206003027/http://www.tatamotors.com/our_world/rearview.php?version=text|archivedate=6 December 2010}}</ref>

In 1999, Tata Motors entered talks to sell its struggling passenger car business, and [[Ford Motor Company|Ford]] emerged as a potential buyer. However, after meeting Ford chairperson [[William Clay Ford Jr.|Bill Ford]] in Detroit, [[Ratan Tata]] decided not to sell the business.<ref name="thehindu.com">{{Cite news |last= |date=2024-10-10 |title=How Ratan Tata bailed out Ford by buying Jaguar-Land Rover, despite the American firm humiliating him years before |url=https://www.thehindu.com/business/Industry/how-ratan-tata-bailed-out-ford-by-buying-jaguar-land-rover-despite-the-american-firm-humiliating-him-years-before/article68740015.ece |access-date=2024-11-08 |work=The Hindu |language=en-IN |issn=0971-751X}}</ref><ref name="ndtv.com">{{Cite web |title=The Jaguar Land Rover Story: How Ratan Tata Triumphed After Ford Snub |url=https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/ratan-tata-death-jaguar-land-rover-ford-the-jaguar-land-rover-story-how-ratan-tata-triumphed-after-ford-snub-6758368 |access-date=2024-11-08 |website=NDTV.com}}</ref>

Later in 2008, during the [[Great Recession]], Ford verged on bankruptcy. Tata offered to buy their [[Jaguar Land Rover]] (JLR) for $2.3 billion. Bill Ford reportedly thanked Tata by saying "You are doing us a big favour by buying JLR."<ref name="thehindu.com"/><ref name="ndtv.com"/><ref name="media.ford.com">{{cite press release |title=Ford Motor Company Announces Agreement to Sell Jaguar Land Rover to Tata Motors |publisher=Ford Motor Company |date=26 March 2008 |url=http://media.ford.com/newsroom/release_display.cfm?release=27953 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080612192629/http://media.ford.com/newsroom/release_display.cfm?release=27953 |archive-date=12 June 2008 |access-date=27 March 2008}}</ref><ref name="definitive1">{{cite press release |title=Tata Motors enters into Definitive Agreement with Ford for purchase of Jaguar Land Rover |publisher=Tata Motors |date=26 March 2008 |url=http://www.tatamotors.com/our_world/press_releases.php?ID=356&action=Pull |access-date=27 March 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101205235956/http://www.tatamotors.com/our_world/press_releases.php?ID=356&action=Pull |archive-date=5 December 2010 }}</ref><ref name="communications1">{{cite news |title=Classic names are part of Tata deal |first=Tony |last=Lewin |date=27 March 2008 |url=http://www.autonews.com/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=/20080327/COPY01/803239/1193 |publisher=Crain Communications |work=Automotive News |access-date=18 May 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080328212307/http://www.autonews.com/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=%2F20080327%2FCOPY01%2F803239%2F1193 |archive-date=28 March 2008 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="r_20080602">{{cite news |title=Tata Motors completes acquisition of Jag, Land Rover |date=2 June 2008 |publisher=Thomson Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/ousiv/idUSBMA00084220080602 |access-date=2 June 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081229000957/http://www.reuters.com/article/ousiv/idUSBMA00084220080602 |archive-date=29 December 2008 |url-status=live }}</ref> 

[[File:Nano.jpg|thumb|Tata Nano]]
In January 2008, Tata Motors launched [[Tata Nano]], the least expensive production car in the world at about {{INR}}120,000 ({{USD}}3,000).<ref name="forbes.com">{{cite news|url=https://www.forbes.com/home/free_forbes/2007/0416/070.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070501110440/http://www.forbes.com/home/free_forbes/2007/0416/070.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=1 May 2007|title=The Next People's Car|accessdate=21 January 2008|work=Forbes|date=16 April 2007}}</ref> The [[city car]] was unveiled during the Auto Expo 2008 exhibition in [[Pragati Maidan]], [[New Delhi]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/articleshowpics/2689238.cms
|title= Time to say hi to Tata's dream car |work=The Times of India | date=10 January 2008}}</ref>

Tata faced controversy over developing the Nano, as environmentalists like Anumita Roychoudhury of the Centre for Science and Environment in Delhi<ref>Fred Attewill , [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2008/jan/10/india.climatechange "World's cheapest car upsets environmentalists"], ''The Guardian'', 10 January 2008</ref> and [[Rajendra K. Pachauri]],<ref>Gavin Rabinowitz, [http://usatoday30.usatoday.com/money/autos/2008-01-10-2500-car_N.htm "Carmaker in India unveils $2,500 car"], ''USA Today'', October 2008</ref> the chairperson of the [[Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change]] (IPCC), raised concerns over the launch of such a low-priced car which could lead to [[Tata Nano#Mass motorization and climate change|mass motorization]] in India, leading to an increase in pollution and accelerate [[climate change]].<ref>Colin Mathews, [http://www.thecarconnection.com/news/1019626_tata-nano-hits-the-market-environmentalists-sound-alarm "Tata Nano Hits The Market, Environmentalists Sound Alarm"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714125018/http://www.thecarconnection.com/news/1019626_tata-nano-hits-the-market-environmentalists-sound-alarm |date=14 July 2014 }}, ''The Car Connection'', 23 March 2009</ref><ref>Siddhartha Shome, [http://thebreakthrough.org/archive/the_little_car_that_environmen "The Little Car that Environmentalists Love to Hate"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140528082810/http://thebreakthrough.org/archive/the_little_car_that_environmen |date=28 May 2014 }}, ''The Breakthrough'', January 2008</ref> Tata had set up a factory in [[Sanand]], [[Gujarat]], and the first Nanos were rolled out in the summer of 2009.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thehindu.com/business/companies/tata-motors-acquire-ford-india-sanand-plant-in-gujarat-to-expand-production-capacity/article65744732.ece|title=Tata Motors to acquire Ford India's Sanand plant to expand production capacity|date=8 August 2022|via=www.thehindu.com}}</ref>

At the 12th [[Auto Expo]] in February 2014, Tata Motors unveiled The Bolt, a [[hatchback]] and The Zest, a compact [[Sedan (automobile)|sedan]].<ref>[http://www.autocarindia.com/auto-news/auto-expo-2014-tata-bolt-hatchback-and-tata-zest-sedan-unveiled-371212.aspx "Auto Expo 2014: Tata Bolt hatchback and Tata Zest sedan unveiled"], ''Autocar India'', 3 February 2014</ref>

In 2015, Tata Motors Cars entered the Southeast Asian market by expanding into Vietnam and the Philippines.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/tata-motors-forays-into-vietnam/articleshow/47300843.cms|title=Tata Motors forays into Vietnam|date=15 May 2015|via=The Economic Times - The Times of India}}</ref>

Tata Motors increased its [[utility vehicle]] [[market share]] to over 8% in FY2019.<ref>{{cite news | url= https://www.autocarpro.in/analysis-sales/tata-motors-increases-its-uv-market-share-to-over-8-in-fy2019-42688?hqcountry=India | title=Tata Motors Market Share | work=Auto Car Professional | access-date=2 April 2019}}</ref>

On 12 October 2021, private equity firm [[TPG Inc.|TPG]] invested $1 billion in Tata Motors' electric vehicle subsidiary.<ref name="Barman 2021">{{cite web | last=Barman | first=Arijit | title=TPG - Tata Motors: TPG drives into Tata Motors EV business with $1 billion investment | website=The Economic Times | date=12 October 2021 | url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/renewables/tpg-drives-into-tata-motors-ev-business-with-1-billion-investment/articleshow/86966881.cms | access-date=13 October 2021}}</ref>

In May 2022, Tata Motors acquired [[Ford India]]'s [[Sanand]] manufacturing plant.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Livemint |date=2022-05-30 |title=Tata Motors to acquire Ford India's Sanand plant |url=https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/tata-motors-to-acquire-ford-india-s-sanand-plant-11653886406603.html |access-date=2022-06-02 |website=mint |language=en}}</ref>

In 2024, Tata Motors announced the demerger of [[Tata Motors|its commercial vehicles business]]. The demerger was completed in October 2025.<ref>{{cite news |title=Tata Motors says commercial vehicles unit to be renamed as Tata Motors Limited |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/auto/auto-news/tata-motors-says-tml-commercial-vehicles-to-be-renamed-tata-motors-limited/articleshow/124426811.cms |access-date=29 November 2025 |work=The Economic Times |date=9 October 2025}}</ref>

== Operations ==
{{See also|Sanand Plant (Tata Motors)}}
Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles makes products in the compact, midsize car, and utility vehicle segments.<ref name="tatamotors1">{{cite web |url=http://www.tatamotors.com/our_world/profile.php |title=Tata Motors |publisher=Tata Motors |access-date=4 June 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110111233915/http://www.tatamotors.com/our_world/profile.php |archive-date=11 January 2011 }}</ref> The company's manufacturing plants in India are in Pune (Maharashtra) and Sanand (Gujarat). Tata's dealership, sales, service, and spare parts network comprise over 3,500 touchpoints.<ref name="tatamotors1"/> Tata Motors has more than 250 dealerships in more than 195 cities across 27 [[States of India|states]] and four [[Union Territory|Union Territories]] of India.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://tatanano.inservices.tatamotors.com/tatamotors/index.php?option=com_booking&task=outlets&Itemid=304 |title=Booking Center Locator |website=tatanano.inservices.tatamotors.com |access-date=15 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090325045013/http://tatanano.inservices.tatamotors.com/tatamotors/index.php?option=com_booking&task=outlets&Itemid=304 |archive-date=25 March 2009 |url-status=dead}}</ref> It has the third-largest sales and service network after [[Maruti Suzuki]] and [[Hyundai Motor India Limited|Hyundai]].

Tata also has franchisee/joint venture assembly operations in Kenya, Bangladesh, Ukraine, Russia, and Senegal.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.tatacarsworldwide.com/company/index.asp |title=Tata Motors International : Company : Profile |publisher=Tatacarsworldwide.com |access-date=4 June 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090304153342/http://www.tatacarsworldwide.com/company/index.asp |archive-date=4 March 2009 |url-status=live }}</ref> Tata has dealerships in 26 countries across 4 continents.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.tatacarsworldwide.com/global-presence/index.asp |title=Tata Motors International : Global Network |publisher=Tatacarsworldwide.com |access-date=4 June 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090715091655/http://www.tatacarsworldwide.com/global-presence/index.asp |archive-date=15 July 2009 |url-status=live }}</ref> Tata is present in many countries, it has managed to create a large consumer base in the [[Indian subcontinent]], namely India, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Sri Lanka and Nepal. Tata is also present in Italy,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tatamotors.it/|title=Tata Motors -|website=Tata Motors|access-date=27 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170527185710/http://tatamotors.it/|archive-date=27 May 2017|url-status=live}}</ref> Spain,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.tatamotors.es/ |title=Tata Motors España. Coches Tata - Coches Nuevos y Nuevas Ofertas de Tata |publisher=Tatamotors.es |access-date=28 June 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071011014019/http://www.tatamotors.es/ |archive-date=11 October 2007 |url-status=live }}</ref> Poland,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://tatamotor.com.pl/|title=Start - sklep internetowy Tata Motors POLSKA |website=tatamotor.com.pl|access-date=27 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170928150018/https://www.tatamotor.com.pl/|archive-date=28 September 2017|url-status=live}}</ref> Romania,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.davossi.ro/ |title=Davossi |publisher=Davossi.ro |access-date=28 June 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150801064425/http://davossi.ro/ |archive-date=1 August 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Turkey,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.tata.com.tr/ |title=Tata Türkıye |publisher=Tata.com.tr |access-date=28 June 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080112000231/http://www.tata.com.tr/ |archive-date=12 January 2008 |url-status=live }}</ref> Chile,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.tata-motors.cl/ |title=Tata Motors |publisher=Tata-motors.cl |access-date=28 June 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110809092821/http://www.tata-motors.cl/ |archive-date=9 August 2011 |url-status=live }}</ref> South Africa,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.tata.co.za/ |title=Tata Homepage - Tata South Africa |publisher=Tata.co.za |access-date=28 June 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150626234455/http://www.tata.co.za/ |archive-date=26 June 2015 |url-status=live }}</ref> Oman, Kuwait, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Iraq, Syria and Australia.

=== Jaguar Land Rover ===
{{Main|Jaguar Land Rover}}

[[File:Land Rover Range Rover Autobiography 2016.jpg|thumb|[[Range Rover (L405)]]]]
[[File:Land Rover Defender (L663) Auto Zuerich 2021 IMG 0431.jpg| thumb |249x249px| right | alt= Land Rover Defender  |
Land Rover Defender]]
[[Jaguar Land Rover]] (JLR) is a premium British automaker headquartered in [[Whitley, Coventry]], United Kingdom, and has been a wholly owned subsidiary of Tata Motors since June 2008, when it acquired the two brands from the American [[Ford Motor Company]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Rutherford |first=Mike |date=29 March 2008 |title=Mike Rutherford ponders Tata's takeover of Land Rover and Jaguar |work=The Daily Telegraph |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/motoring/main.jhtml?xml=/motoring/2008/03/29/mrmoney129.xml |url-status=dead |access-date=30 July 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080408233420/http://www.telegraph.co.uk/motoring/main.jhtml?xml=%2Fmotoring%2F2008%2F03%2F29%2Fmrmoney129.xml |archive-date=8 April 2008}}</ref> Its principal activity is the development, manufacture and sale of [[Jaguar Cars|Jaguar]] luxury and sports cars and [[Land Rover]] premium four-wheel-drive vehicles.

JLR has two design centres and three assembly plants in the United Kingdom. Under Tata ownership, JLR has launched new vehicles including the [[Range Rover Evoque]], [[Jaguar F-Type]], the [[Jaguar XE]], the [[Jaguar XJ (X351)]], the second-generation [[Range Rover Sport]], and [[Jaguar XF]], the fourth-generation [[Land Rover Discovery]], [[Range Rover Velar]]  and the [[Range Rover (L405)]].
[[File:2019 Land Rover Discovery Sport R-Dynamic SE 2.0 Front.jpg|thumb|[[Land Rover Discovery Sport]]]]
[[File:2017 Jaguar F-Type V6 R-Dynamic Automatic 3.0 Front.jpg|thumb|[[Jaguar F-Type]]]]
JD Power, of the US, rates Land Rover and Jaguar as the two worst brands for initial quality.
<ref>{{cite news |last=McIntyre |first=Douglas A. |date=24 June 2019 |title=And the Worst New Car Sold in America Is… |work=MSN |publisher=Microsoft News |url=https://www.msn.com/en-us/autos/news/and-the-worst-new-car-sold-in-america-is%e2%80%a6/ar-AADlFYP?ocid=spartanntp |access-date=25 June 2019}}</ref> The Jaguar F-Pace made [[Consumer Reports]] February 2019 list of the 10 Least Reliable Cars. The editors cited "electronics, drive system, power equipment, noises and leaks" as problematic aspects.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Linkov |first1=Jon |last2=Elek |first2=Steven |date=18 November 2021 |title=10 Least Reliable Cars |url=https://www.consumerreports.org/car-reliability-owner-satisfaction/10-least-reliable-cars/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191007021807/https://www.consumerreports.org/car-reliability-owner-satisfaction/10-least-reliable-cars/ |archive-date=7 October 2019 |work=Consumer Reports}}</ref>
   
JLR was struggling by 2019 and Tata Motors wrote down its investment in JLR by $3.9 billion. Much of the financial problem was due to a 50% drop in sales in China during 2019, although the situation was improving. Still, Tata was open to considering a partnership with another company according to a statement in mid-October, as long as the partnership agreement would allow Tata to maintain control of the business. The company ruled out the possibility of a sale of JLR to another entity.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Trudell |first1=Craig |last2=Coppola |first2=Gabrielle |last3=Kotoky |first3=Anurag |date=15 October 2019 |title=Tata Looks for Jaguar Land Rover Partners, but Rules Out Sale |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2019-10-15/tata-chairman-awaiting-brexit-deal-says-tariffs-are-new-normal |url-access=subscription |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191017184321/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2019-10-15/tata-chairman-awaiting-brexit-deal-says-tariffs-are-new-normal |archive-date=17 October 2019 |work=Bloomberg}}</ref>

In July 2023, the Tata Group announced its plans to invest £4 billion to build an electric car battery factory in the UK, which will be one of the largest of its kind in Europe.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tata Group confirms plans to build gigafactory for batteries in the UK |url=https://news.sky.com/story/tata-motors-to-build-electric-car-battery-factory-in-uk-12923165 |access-date=2023-07-20 |website=Sky News |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Ralph |first=Alex |date=2023-07-20 |title=Tata to build £4bn gigafactory in Somerset |language=en |newspaper=[[The Times]] |url=https://www.thetimes.com/article/tata-to-build-gigafactory-in-somerset-knpvqclxd |access-date=2023-07-20 |issn=0140-0460}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite news |date=2024-02-28 |title=Tata confirms Somerset will host £4bn battery factory |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-somerset-68412570 |access-date=2024-02-28 |work=BBC News |language=en-GB}}</ref> The factory will be the first facility operated by the group's battery manufacturing subsidiary, Agratas, outside India.<ref name=":1" /> Located in [[Bridgwater]], Somerset, the factory will supply future battery electric Jaguar and Land Rover models, with the potential to also supply other car manufacturers.<ref name=":0" /> Production at the new facility is due to start in 2026.

=== Electric vehicles ===
'''Tata Passenger Electric Mobility''' is a subsidiary which produces electric cars under the brand name Tata Motors.<ref name="auto"/>

Tata Motors unveiled electric versions of the [[Tata Indica EV|Tata Indica]] passenger car powered by TM4 electric motors and inverters,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.tm4.com/about-us/customers/ |title=Customers |publisher=TM4 |access-date=28 June 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150630233327/http://tm4.com/about-us/customers/ |archive-date=30 June 2015 |url-status=live }}</ref> and running on lithium batteries.
[[File:Tata EVision, GIMS 2018, Le Grand-Saconnex (1X7A1191).jpg|thumb|Tata EVision concept (2018)]]
In 2008 Tata Motors' UK subsidiary, Tata Motors European Technical Centre, bought a 50.3% holding in [[electric vehicle]] technology firm Miljøbil Grenland/Innovasjon of Norway for {{USD}}1.93 million, and planned to launch the electric Indica hatchback in Europe the following year.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.tata.com/media/releases/inside.aspx?artid=D8J398/KAjI= |title=TMETC acquires 50.3 per cent stake in Norway's Miljo Grenland/Innovasjon; to launch first electric vehicle |publisher=Tata.com |date=14 October 2008 |access-date=2 May 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130730110821/http://www.tata.com/media/releases/inside.aspx?artid=D8J398%2FKAjI%3D |archive-date=30 July 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.tata.com/company/profile.aspx?sectid=MiEz+LbA1Yg= |title=Tata Motors European Technical Centre |publisher=Tata.com |access-date=2 May 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090124131750/http://tata.com/company/profile.aspx?sectid=MiEz+LbA1Yg= |archive-date=24 January 2009 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.just-auto.com/article.aspx?id=96329&lk=dm |title=Tata to launch EV next year |publisher=Just-auto.com |date=14 October 2008 |access-date=2 May 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090329062948/http://www.just-auto.com/article.aspx?id=96329&lk=dm |archive-date=29 March 2009 |url-status=live }}</ref>

In December 2019, Tata Motors unveiled the Nexon EV, an SUV with a 30.2 kWh lithium-ion battery and a consistent range of 312 km on a single charge. It is also equipped with fast charging technology, which can charge the vehicle from 0% - 80% in 60 minutes.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Tata Nexon EV - India's Own Electric Compact SUV Powered by Ziptron|url=https://nexonev.tatamotors.com/|access-date=28 July 2020|website=Tata Nexon EV - India's Own Electric Compact SUV Powered by Ziptron|language=en}}</ref>

Tata announced the [[Avinya]] brand of premium electric vehicles in November 2023, to be launched in 2026 using JLR's Electrified Modular Architecture.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.businessworld.in/article/tata-motors-partners-with-jlr-for-avinya-electric-car-development-497416|title=Tata Motors Partners With JLR For Avinya Electric Car Development|date=3 November 2023|access-date=9 July 2026|work=Businessworld}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.autocarindia.com/car-news/tata-avinya-to-be-underpinned-by-jlr8217s-ema-born-ev-platform-429752|title=Tata Avinya to be underpinned by JLR’s EMA born EV platform|date=2 November 2023|access-date=9 July 2026|work=Autocar India}}</ref> After a delay to 2027, in June 2026, Tata agreed to license a platform developed by Chinese automaker [[Chery]] for the [[Freelander 8]] produced by [[Chery Jaguar Land Rover|Chery JLR]], to be used in the brand's vehicles; Tata will assemble vehicles in a [[Panapakkam]] facility from Chinese [[knock-down kit]]s made by Chery.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.reuters.com/world/china/indias-tata-taps-chinas-chery-premium-ev-push-sources-say-2026-06-03/|title=India's Tata taps Chery for premium EV push, leveraging Chinese tech|date=3 June 2026|access-date=10 July 2026|work=Reuters|last=Shah|first=Aditi}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.electrive.com/2026/06/03/india-tata-motors-to-license-chery-jlrs-freelander-platform/|title=India: Tata Motors to license Chery JLR’s Freelander platform|date=3 June 2026|access-date=10 July 2026|work=Electrive|last=Parikh|first=Sagar}}</ref>

=== Tata Technologies ===
[[Tata Technologies]] Limited (TTL) is a 43%-owned subsidiary of Tata Motors which provides design, engineering, and [[business process outsourcing]] services to the automotive industry. It is headquartered in [[Pune]]'s [[Hinjawadi|Hinjawadi business district]] and also has operations in London, [[Detroit]] and Thailand. Its clients include Ford, [[General Motors]], [[Honda]], and [[Toyota]].

The British engineering and design services company Incat International, which specialises in engineering and design services and product lifecycle management in the automotive, aerospace, and engineering sectors, is a wholly owned subsidiary of TTL. It was acquired by TTL in August 2005 for {{INR}}4 billion.

In 2017, TAL, a subsidiary of Tata Motors, manufactured India's first industrial articulated robot for micro, small, and medium enterprises.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|url=http://www.thehindu.com/news/national/robotic-hand-rocks-manufacturing-cradle/article17934526.ece?homepage=true|title=Robotic hand rocks manufacturing cradle|last=Mondal|first=Manisha|work=The Hindu|access-date=11 April 2017|language=en}}</ref>

=== Stellantis partnership ===
{{see also|Fiat India Automobiles}}
[[Fiat India Automobiles]] is an India-based joint venture between Tata and [[Stellantis]] (formerly [[Fiat S.p.A.|Fiat]], then [[Fiat Chrysler Automobiles|FCA]]) which produces Jeep and Tata branded passenger cars, as well as engines and transmissions. Tata Motors has gained access to Fiat's [[diesel engine]] and [[Transmission (mechanics)|transmission]] technology through the joint venture.<ref name="timesofmalta.com">{{cite web|url=http://www.timesofmalta.com/motoring/view/20071021/news/fiat-tata-motors-set-up-joint-venture|title=Fiat, Tata Motors set up joint venture|access-date=1 April 2008|date=21 October 2007|work=timesofmalta.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071118071457/http://www.timesofmalta.com/motoring/view/20071021/news/fiat-tata-motors-set-up-joint-venture|archive-date=18 November 2007|url-status=live}}</ref>

The two companies formerly also had a distribution joint venture through which Fiat products were sold in India through joint Tata-Fiat dealerships. This distribution arrangement was ended in March 2013; Stellantis cars have since been distributed in India by [[Stellantis India]], a wholly owned subsidiary of Stellantis.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/fiat-to-complete-split-from-tata-in-sales-ops-by-mar-2013-112091900131_1.html|title=Fiat to complete split from Tata in sales ops by Mar 2013|access-date=12 January 2014|publisher=Business Standard|date=19 September 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140112230837/http://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/fiat-to-complete-split-from-tata-in-sales-ops-by-mar-2013-112091900131_1.html|archive-date=12 January 2014|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com/2013-04-11/news/38463206_1_tata-fiat-jv-tata-motors-outlets|title=After split with Tata Motors, Fiat begins its solo India ride|access-date=12 January 2014|publisher=The Economic Times|date=11 April 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140112190230/http://articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com/2013-04-11/news/38463206_1_tata-fiat-jv-tata-motors-outlets|archive-date=12 January 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref>

=== Tata Motors Design Tech Centre ===
The '''Tata Motors Design Tech Centre''', formerly known as the '''Tata Motors European Technical Centre''', is an automotive design, engineering, and research company based at [[WMG, University of Warwick]] on the campus of the [[University of Warwick]] in England. It was established in 2005.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.motorbeam.com/news/tata-news/tata-motors-unveils-new-range-of-trucks/ |title=Tata Motors Unveils New Range Of Trucks |publisher=Motorbeam.com |date=29 May 2009 |access-date=4 June 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090601071947/http://www.motorbeam.com/news/tata-news/tata-motors-unveils-new-range-of-trucks/ |archive-date=1 June 2009 }}</ref>

In September 2013, it was announced that a new [[National Automotive Innovation Campus]] would be built at WMG at Warwick's main campus at a cost of £100 million.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/student/news/100m-investment-boost-for-warwick-university-8839352.html|title=£100m investment boost for Warwick University|access-date=29 September 2013|work=The Independent|date=25 September 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130929184819/http://www.independent.co.uk/student/news/100m-investment-boost-for-warwick-university-8839352.html|archive-date=29 September 2013|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-coventry-warwickshire-24227662|title=University of Warwick £100m car centre 'will secure jobs'|access-date=29 September 2013|publisher=BBC|date=24 September 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130928174356/http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-coventry-warwickshire-24227662|archive-date=28 September 2013|url-status=live}}</ref> The initiative will be a partnership between Tata Motors, the university, and Jaguar Land Rover, with £30 million in funding coming from Tata Motors.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.theengineer.co.uk/channels/policy-and-business/news/tata-motors-confirms-30m-in-uk-rd-centre/1017613.article|title=Tata Motors confirms £30m investment in UK R&D centre|access-date=27 February 2014|publisher=The Engineer|date=3 December 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141129035627/http://www.theengineer.co.uk/channels/policy-and-business/news/tata-motors-confirms-30m-in-uk-rd-centre/1017613.article|archive-date=29 November 2014}}</ref>
